title: normalize-sdk-credential-shape-and-stream-signatures-across-py-ts-go
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Harmonized credential object fields across SDKs (client_id -> clientId alias added)
- Unified streaming call signatures and ergonomic aliases (pullStream / streamAsync)
- Minor version bumps: python v1.14.0, typescript v1.28.0, go v1.9.3
- Backwards-compatible shims for existing call sites; runtime warnings for deprecated names
description:
Summary: This PR aligns credential payload shapes and streaming call signatures in the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to reduce cross-language friction for customers and internal examples. Motivation: multiple docs and examples were diverging (camelCase vs snake_case credential fields; different async/iterator ergonomics for streaming). The change set standardizes on a compact, explicit credential shape and adds lightweight compatibility shims so existing call sites continue to work.

Goals:
- Standardize on a superset credential object with stable aliases (clientId, client_id, token, api_key)
- Provide identical streaming entrypoints: pull_stream / pullStream / StreamPull with consistent semantics across SDKs
- Keep runtime behavior backward-compatible; emit deprecation warnings rather than hard errors
- Keep changes small in surface area; prefer shims and adapters over mass API renames

What changed (high level):
- Python: redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/credentials.py: introduce CredentialSpec class, add from_mapping helper, add deprecated alias properties for camelCase fields. Update streaming client in streaming.py to accept both generator/callable and async iterator payloads; add pull_stream alias.
- TypeScript: packages/redwood-sdk-typescript/src/credentials.ts: export CredentialLike type, create normalizeCredential() helper. streaming.ts: expose pullStream function and async iterator compatibility layer; update JSDoc to show normalized examples.
- Go: sdk/go/credentials/cred.go: introduce Credential struct with json tags for both camelCase and snake_case; normalize in NewCredentialFromMap. stream/client.go: add StreamPull convenience wrapper that returns a channel-based consumer and implements io.Closer for ergonomic shutdown.
- Tests: unit tests added for normalization, streaming adapters, and cross-language example snippets ported to each SDK's test suite.
- Docs: update quickstart snippets in redwood-examples/docs/ to use normalized credential fields and demonstrate both alias forms.

Commit summary:
- feat(cred): add CredentialSpec and normalization helpers in py/ts/go
- feat(stream): add pull_stream/pullStream/StreamPull ergonomic wrappers
- test: add unit tests for credential aliases and streaming adapters
- docs: update quickstarts and examples
- ci: fix go vet and regenerate lockfile for ts SDK

Changed files (representative):
- redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/credentials.py
- redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/streaming.py
- redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_credentials_normalize.py
- packages/redwood-sdk-typescript/src/credentials.ts
- packages/redwood-sdk-typescript/src/streaming.ts
- packages/redwood-sdk-typescript/test/credentials.spec.ts
- sdk/go/credentials/cred.go
- sdk/go/stream/client.go
- redwood-examples/docs/quickstart-cred.md

Small illustrative snippets (kept intentionally short):
Python normalization helper usage:
cred = CredentialSpec.from_mapping({"clientId": "abc", "token": "xyz"})
# cred.client_id and cred.clientId both available (clientId is deprecated alias)

TypeScript example:
const cred = normalizeCredential({ client_id: 'abc', api_key: 'xyz' });
for await (const chunk of pullStream(model, request, cred)) { console.log(chunk); }

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Please ensure the deprecation warnings are rate-limited and not noisy in high-throughput services. Also add a clear migration note for customers using direct dict-style creds in python."
  - Maya Chen (author): "Agreed — added a DeprecationLogger singleton that emits one warning per process per deprecated field; updated py docs with migration section."

- Sonia Lopez (reviewer): "Go wrapper looks good but go vet complained about unused imports in client.go on the first CI run. Also request explicit Close() guidance in docs to avoid goroutine leaks."
  - Maya Chen: "Addressed: removed unused imports, added Close() example in go/README.md, and added a test that verifies no goroutines leak on stream Close()."

- Ethan Brooks (reviewer): "TypeScript: please ensure types keep backward compatibility — adding a CredentialLike union is better than replacing the type entirely."
  - Maya Chen: "Done — CredentialLike union added and exported; existing code paths compile without changes."

CI runs: 
- Initial run: typescript lint + python unit tests passed; go build failed (unused import in client.go)
- Follow-up run: fixed imports, initial failing Go test added more strictness; adjusted test harness, all checks passed
- Final CI: all checks (lint/test/build) passed, coverage delta +0.2%

Compatibility notes and migration guidance: 
- Existing code using client_id or clientId will continue to work; the SDK will log a single deprecation warning per process for the deprecated key.
- Streaming: old streaming helpers still present but the preferred ergonomic interfaces are the new pull_stream / pullStream wrappers — they are thin adapters over existing code.
- Version bumps: this PR also includes coordinated version bumps for the three SDKs to make the release easier for downstream dependents.

Merge details: squashed and merged to main after reviewers approved; changelog entry added to releases/notes. Merged by Sonia Lopez on 2025-06-18 (merge method: squash).

Notes for release engineers: tag python v1.14.0, typescript v1.28.0, go v1.9.3. Coordinate minor advisory e-mail for customers who pinned older SDK versions and rely on raw dict credential shapes.

If follow-ups are needed I recommend:
- a small telemetry PR to capture how many customers still use deprecated fields (low-overhead sampling),
- a docs-only PR to add side-by-side examples for every major language, and
- consider a major deprecation policy doc to make eventual removal less surprising.
